newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine PM to decide on reform chief's fate.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine PM to decide on reform chief's fate.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma has ordered his prime minister to decide whether to accept the resignation of a top economic reformer who quit in anger this week, Kuchma's press service said on Friday.
Viktor Pynzenyk, deputy prime minister in charge of the economy and a leading reformer popular with Western funding bodies, said in his resignation letter he was angry at the slow speed of reforms.

"A decision has not been made yet. The president simply wants to know the prime minister's recommendation and only then will he make a decision on the matter," Kuchma's deputy spokesman Serhiy Kutsiy told Reuters.
Pynzenyk's aides said the 42-year-old economics professor from western Ukraine was also angry with the long-delayed budget, which the largely conservative parliament is due to review this month.
Kutsiy said that, in keeping with Ukraine's constitution, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko would recommend to the president appointments and dismissals of deputy prime ministers and ministers.

Passage of the budget, together with a package of tax reform laws, would pave the way for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to deliver a $2.5 to $3 billion three-year credit to the former Soviet republic.
Kutsiy added that Kuchma met with Lazarenko on Thursday to discuss changes in the cabinet.
Ukraine has never passed a budget on time since independence in 1991.
It has yet to report economic growth and has attracted only $1.4 billion in foreign investment more than five years after independence from the Soviet Union.
